chunks: Al-Shaykh (al-Mufid), may God the Exalted support him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban — both — from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him)
he said: «Wudu is not made obligatory except from defecation, or urine, or audible flatulence, or silent flatulence whose odor is perceived.»

key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: defecation — the primary and universally agreed nullifier of wudu
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu — ritual ablution required before salat; 'is made obligatory' here means it is nullified and must be renewed
key_terms.ضَرْطَةٍ: audible flatulence — passing wind with sound, legally distinguished from the silent form
key_terms.فَسْوَةٍ: silent flatulence — passing wind without sound but with perceivable odor; both forms are nullifiers according to this hadith

ai.seo_question: What are the four things that nullify wudu according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) enumerates precisely four bodily occurrences that nullify wudu and make its renewal obligatory: defecation, urination, audible flatulence (darta), and silent flatulence detected by odor (faswa). This hadith is a foundational jurisprudential text in Shia fiqh for defining the nullifiers (nawaqid) of ritual purity, and carries special authority as it is transmitted through Zurara ibn A'yan, one of the most trusted companions of the Imam.
